recipes.name: Spumoni Chocolate Chip Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant pistachio pudding mix

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Sift flour and baking soda together; set aside.
Beat butter, brown sugar, and white sugar together in a large bowl until smooth.
Stir in pudding mix until well combined. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla.
Stir in flour mixture, then fold in chocolate chips, cherries, and pistachios.
Drop large spoonfuls of dough onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until light brown, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spumoni Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This spumoni chocolate chip cookie recipe is an Italian-inspired twist on an American tradition—cherries and pistachios liven up chocolate chip cookies.

review.reviewBody: I've never had a recipe my family asks me to make more than this! We live in different states and every time I come "home" to visit, I know they expect me to bring a fresh batch of cookies along with! Even my brother, who can be somewhat hard to please, raves about these delicious spumoni chocolate chip cookies!! A must-try!

I loved this recipe! It was a huge hit with my twin brother!! I did make several changes to the recipe, though. I used two 3.4 oz packages of the pudding mix, I only used 2 cups of the flour, and right after stirring in the vanilla in the butter-pudding mix mixture, I added to it two drops of green food coloring. Oh, and here are a few things to help out my fellow bakers with this recipe: *approximately 49 pistachio nut meats=1/4 cup of chopped pistachios, *10 maraschino cherries=1/2 cup chopped maraschino cherries, *and you can substitute 1 1/4 cups chocolate morsels (which are slightly larger than regular-sized chocolate chips) for the chocolate chips in this recipe.

Made these for a second time because we liked them a lot, but felt the chocolate was overwhelming the cherries and pistachios. This time we doubled the cherries (16 oz. jar), tripled the pistachios, and cut the chocolate chips in half. Also added in a few drops of green food coloring. Even added a pistachio on top. Now they’re even better!

This is everything you could want in a cookie! Tender and chewy on the inside, just-right-crispy on the outside, sweet and slightly salty, and a beautiful presentation. I tried these today as a test run before bringing them to my office hoiday party. Beautiful and delicous. I used all white sugar and two boxes of instant pistachio mix. Tip: Use a scoop for uniform cookies and roll in the palms of your hands to smooth before baking. This recipe is sure to be a hit - it's a keeper.

A wonderful twist on a classic! I used an entire 12 oz jar of cherries and chopped them well, also used a 12 oz pkg of chocolate chips. Nice, soft cookies with a very light green tint. I used a Pampered Chef medium cookie scoop and it yielded 40 cookies. If making for the holidays, you may want to add a couple drops of green food coloring to make them a stronger green color and extra Christmas-y!

I have been making this recipe for 15 years!! I make it every year at Christmas time. I make tweaks to mine as well. I add a bit more chopped cherries, I also include 2 TBS of the juice. I add more chopped pistachios as well. To give it more of a cherry flavor I add 1-2 TSP of Almond Extract. We love this cookie.. Christmas time comes around and I crave it. It makes a lot! A MUST!

Just made these cookies and used some of the other reviews using two puddings, less flour. Reason for four stars is the cooking time was off. Had a hard time determining what worked and what I would do next. Cooking time I used 14-15 minutes and I would flatten a bit before cooking. Otherwise, the taste was great!

The first time I made these, I followed the recipe exactly except for using an entire 10 oz jar of maraschino cherries (because what was I going to do with the leftovers?)... it's only an extra 1/4 cup anyway. the chocolate chips were a little challenging, since there's no such thing as a 16 oz bag - did the author mean 12 oz bag or 2 and 1/2 cups? I went with the 12 oz bag. People really liked them, but I thought they could be improved. I replaced the vanilla flavoring with almond, added another pistachio pudding mix and used 3 cups of chocolate chips. Everyone agreed that they were even better with those revisions.

These are a wonderful variation to chocolate chip cookies, but do taste more like a chocolate chip cookie with a hint of cherry and pistachio. In order to balance the three flavors, I made the following modifications - 1) CHOCOLATE CHIPS - reduced to 6oz (half a bag), 2) CHERRIES - increased to 3/4 cup, 3) PISTACHIOS - increased to 1/2 cup (probably 2 tablespoons were very fine / powder to increase the pistachio flavor), 4) FLOUR - reduced to 2 cups (based on other reviews and because some of the pistachios were chopped fine into a powder).

These were fantastic! I adjusted the recipe for a special Christmas cookie. I split the dough in half, put the cherries in one half and colored it pink, and colored the other half green with almond flavoring and pistachio nuts. Then I split a bag of mini-chips between the 2 halves, and spooned half a scoop of each and put on the cookie sheet. They were great and well-liked!

I made an allrecipes account just so I can post a review for this Spumoni cookie recipe, it is absolutely my favorite cookie recipe!!! The Spumoni flavor brings on so much nostalgia and happiness that this is always the recipe I bring up whenever someone mentions cookies. Im typically required to make at least 7 batches a year as Holiday gifts, they really are a fan favorite! (Not pictured my batches of it!!) A tip: Over time I've learned that letting the chopped cherries sit in a towel for a little bit to absorb some of the juice helps prevent the dough from coming out soggy from too much of the cherry juice, so just keep your eye on it! Thank you for this recipe!!!!

I just finished making these. The flavor is good, but I am disappointed that they are soft, not crispy. I thought that if I used all white sugar instead of the brown sugar, would make the difference. Not sure what happened. I used almond extract instead of vanilla because spumoni ice cream tastes like almonds. The pistachios didn't add anything at all.
I baked our cookies for 11 minutes and they were perfect! Everyone's oven is different, so... No notes other than the time baked.

The batter has a nice taste. I substituted 8-oz chopped candied cherries for the maraschino cherries. Used almond flavoring instead of Vanilla. Also used half a 10-oz bag of chocolate chips. I would prefer to use even less chocolate chips. My husband said they tasted like chocolate chip cookies, but he ate a few of them so he must have thought they were good. The recipe is easy and the consistency of the dough is easy to work with. Cooking time was about 12-15 minutes. Everybody's oven is different. I would make these again, for sure. I might double the pudding mix. It depends on how strong you want that flavor. I rough chopped the nuts.
These had the perfect, soft cookie texture that I love! I would add more pistachios for a stronger pistachio flavor next time. Overall, very good!
Very good! Love the flavor and the cookies turned out very buttery and delicious! How big do you make the individual cookies? I had to bake them for closer to 20 minutes
These were just ok. I have made other versions of the pistachio cherry cookies that tastes better. You really lose all those flavors in this cookie.
really tasty. will go great with spumoni ice cream. we just did 1/2 c. Butter 1/2 c. shortening. 2/3c. maraschino cherries and 1/3 c. chopped pistachios. no big changes. really yummy and creative.

This recipe was a big hit at work. For me it was too many chocolate chips, I think next time I will use half or substitute half with white chocolate. Following the recipe as listed my cookies are very soft and chewy.
